# Infinite Red — account brief

## Who
Infinite Red is a consultancy specializing in React Native app design and development ([source](https://infinitered.com/)). Its GitHub org lists 150 public repos and 2100 followers ([source](https://github.com/infinitered)).

## Production Expo signals
- eas.json is present in infinitered/ignite ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite/blob/main/eas.json))
- react-native 0.74.5 in infinitered/ignite/package.json ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite/blob/main/package.json))
- CI workflows in infinitered/ignite ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite/tree/main/.github/workflows))
- 150 public repos and 2100 followers on the infinitered org ([source](https://github.com/infinitered))

## Why now
infinitered/ignite was last pushed on 2026-08-11, nine days before this brief ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite)). The repo pins react-native 0.74.5 ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite/blob/main/package.json)). The evidence does not include store update cadence or review volume, so store-side recency cannot be assessed.

## Suggested opener
Ignite already ships with an eas.json, so every project scaffolded from it starts on EAS ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite/blob/main/eas.json)). You also run CI workflows in the same repo ([source](https://github.com/infinitered/ignite/tree/main/.github/workflows)). Across client projects started from Ignite, how do you handle builds and store submissions today: EAS end to end, or your own CI pipeline?
